issues.explanation: The entity+owner membership creation and audit logging are a domain write implemented inline in the Livewire component, while the project conventions require one app/Actions/* class per use case with authorization inside the action.

Authorization bypasses the policies/gates: submit() only aborts when unauthenticated, Dashboard::mount() and EntityController::pick() use membershipFor() directly instead of $this->authorize()/policy checks, despite the new EntityPolicy and EntityMembershipPolicy being added for this purpose.

The custom current_entity authorization middleware is attached to the Livewire dashboard route but is never registered with Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware, so it stops running on /livewire/update and the tenant context/403 check only applies to the initial page load.

There is no unauthorized-call or tamper test for the Livewire submit() action (the project's Livewire policy requires both for every action); guest redirects are covered only at HTTP level and ownership tampering is never attempted.

The schema tests check columns and second-owner rejection but never assert the contract's exact index names (entities_slug_unique, entity_memberships_entity_user_unique, entity_memberships_one_owner) or the owner_seq column, so a rename/typo in the migration would pass.

Only the database schema doc was updated; the conventions also require a CHANGELOG entry and keeping docs/architecture.md and docs/business-rules.md in sync with the new tenant context and one-owner invariant.

get(), entity() and has() are never used, and the two container aliases 'tenant'/'current_entity' in app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:19-20 are unused, adding speculative API surface to an otherwise small context class.

isSlugCollision() classifies any SQLSTATE 23000 or message containing 'unique'/'integrity constraint' as a slug collision, so unrelated integrity failures are retried ten times before surfacing, hiding the real error.
The membership fetch with('entity')->filter(entity !== null)->values() block is duplicated in the /home route closure (routes/web.php:23-29) instead of being shared via a relation/scope.
All model, policy, HTTP and Livewire tests sit in one 319-line generic file, making failures harder to locate than per-feature test files.

review.summary: The change implements the entity data model, policies, tenant middleware, onboarding, switcher and dashboard, with broad Pest coverage including the slug-retry, non-member 403 and empty/invalid-session edge cases. It falls short of the project's mandatory Livewire/conventions rules: the domain write bypasses app/Actions, authorization bypasses the policies, and the current_entity middleware is not persisted for Livewire updates, so it needs changes before merging.
